slides.headline: What's the real difference?
slides.body: A business loan provides a single lump sum repaid over a fixed term, suited to a defined purpose like an asset or acquisition. A line of credit provides a standing limit you can draw from, repay and redraw as needed, generally charging interest only on the amount actually drawn.

slides.headline: Certainty or flexibility — both have their place.
slides.body: A defined project may suit a lump-sum loan; ongoing or unpredictable needs may suit a revolving line — subject to lender assessment and approval.

caption:
Not every funding need looks the same, and the right structure depends on the shape of that need.

A business loan gives you a fixed amount for a defined purpose, repaid on a set schedule. A line of credit gives you standing access to draw from, repay and redraw — useful when your capital needs move around rather than sitting still.
